redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_task.py --selftest --stage lo-block` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 5 of 16 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - ae1 (house FAIL), ae4 (house FAIL), ae4 (house FAIL), ae5 (house FAIL), ae6 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 11/16 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: Start snapshot + attribution in _scoped_commit.py: status_paths() reads `git status --porcelain -z --untracked-files=all` (a rename/copy gives both names); path_marks() digests each path in the stamp's dirtyPaths spelling (file_hash prefix, 16 chars); record_attempt()/read_attempt()/drop_attempt() keep <stateDir>/attempts/<taskId>.json (written through _manifest_io.atomic_write_text; a re-start keeps the existing record, done removes it); attribute() sorts paths into predates/during/mixed by the record, else by mtime against startedAt (basis stated), else undated; attempt_strays() applies it to paths no in_progress task covers. uncommitted() now uses status_paths: it used lines(), which strips the blank opening a worktree-only status, so it returned 'M src/a.py' (harmless while only its truth was read). audit-task.py: _porcelain_paths delegates to status_paths (P122-R10). `start` refuses a first start when a declared file is dirty and another blocked/in_progress task with attempts>0 declares it (_held_dirt), naming path and task and offering finish-or-unblock or setting the change aside in a stash named by that task. It records the snapshot and prints it (JSON: startSnapshot). _uncommitted_leftovers returns (left, during, basis); `done --commit` refuses the `during` paths by name with the basis. Bookkeeping and the state/logs dirs are skipped. done drops the snapshot. commit-task-work.py: attempt_refusal() runs before staging. It refuses declared files whose change predates the start (PREDATES), declared files dirty at start and changed since (MIXED, no hunk splitting: refused, not separated), and strays changed during the attempt that no in_progress task covers (offers /audit:task scope or removal). The answer gains an `attempt` key. With no record and more than one recorded attempt, the declared-predates question is not asked. Docs: execute-task.md 4c, verbs-in-full.md start/done, README /audit:task start/done text, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE _scoped_commit section + regenerated module-map fence (only my three edges changed). Tests: test_audit_task lo-block ae1-ae6 (+ lo2/lo4 backdate the uncovered path that now predates; fixture fileIndex accumulates ids); test_commit_task_work ctw-at1..4 (the real start verb), cl1/cl2 fixture writes only the declared file. Runs: lo-block 16/16; test_commit_task_work 97/97; test_audit_task full 967/967; test__scoped_commit 31/31; first full sweep exit 1 (test__deps sw1: os.replace outside sanctioned writers, mine, fixed); second full sweep exit 0, 328/328 files. Not used: the submit stamp's dirtyPaths. No stamp is taken at start (drive-phase takes one only at submit), and it is bounded at 24 paths. start now records an unbounded record in the same digest spelling instead. The pre-existing dirty .claude/hooks/guard-release.py (P123.42-64p) is untouched; with a record it reads as predates and is not blamed.
outcome.descriptive: A task commit and close now carry exactly the attempt. Older dirt in a declared file is refused, not swept in. A file made during the attempt outside every running scope is refused by name. Paths with spaces or non-ASCII bytes are matched.
